questions.q: What is the main problem with a naive server that calls a model's generate function once per incoming request?
options: It cannot run on a GPU at all
It has no batching, scheduling, or memory management, so throughput collapses and latency becomes unpredictable under real traffic
It only works for image models, never for text
It requires no code changes ever
questions.explain: A naive per-request loop processes one request at a time with no batching or continuous scheduling, and no KV cache or admission management, which falls apart under real concurrent load.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four core jobs a dedicated serving framework takes on?
options: Writing the model's training code
Scheduling requests and managing GPU memory for the KV cache efficiently
Collecting payment from end users
Designing the model's neural network architecture
questions.explain: Serving frameworks handle scheduling (deciding which requests run together), memory management (KV cache allocation), execution optimization, and a production-ready interface — not model training or architecture design.

questions.q: Why did LLMs make the need for dedicated serving frameworks more urgent than earlier model types?
options: LLMs never need a GPU
Requests vary wildly in length, decode is inherently sequential, and KV cache memory pressure grows throughout a request's life — none of which earlier, shorter-request model types faced as acutely
LLMs are always smaller than earlier models
Earlier models never needed any serving layer at all
questions.explain: LLM generation introduced variable-length, sequential decode and growing memory pressure from the KV cache, all of which strained naive serving approaches far more than earlier, simpler model types did.

questions.q: What does it mean for a serving framework to expose an "OpenAI-compatible" API?
options: It can only be used with OpenAI's own models
It requires a paid OpenAI subscription
It matches OpenAI's request/response shape, so existing client code written for that format works unmodified
It translates all requests into a proprietary binary format
questions.explain: An OpenAI-compatible API mirrors the familiar request and response structure of OpenAI's API, letting existing client code or tooling work against a different backend without changes.

questions.q: According to this lesson, which three serving frameworks does Chapter 2 cover?
options: TensorFlow Serving, ONNX Runtime, and Ray Serve
vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, and Triton Inference Server
Flask, Django, and FastAPI
PyTorch, TensorFlow, and JAX
questions.explain: Chapter 2 tours vLLM (Lesson 7), TensorRT-LLM (Lesson 8), and Triton Inference Server (Lesson 9), then compares them (Lesson 10) and deploys one (Lesson 11).
